- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.27) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.16), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk reversal or mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the 10–15 day horizon after a spike; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for that window.
- Model overestimates in early horizon (1–5 days) after a sharp price drop; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid “overshoot” bias.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term volatility (e.g., alternating +/–0.11), model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.7% to forecast to capture momentum.
- Model often fails to capture mean reversion in 20+ day horizons; if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to reflect potential rebound.
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model underestimates; apply upward bias of 0.5–1.0% to avoid “bearish trap” bias.
- Model tends to underestimate in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or trending sideways; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for structural drift.
